description: Find the cheapest way to buy a prescription drug in the US, from open data (no key): RxNorm from the National Library of Medicine (brand and generic versions, strengths, package codes), CMS's NADAC (the national average price pharmacies pay, updated weekly) and Mark Cuban Cost Plus Drugs' public price API (a real cash price by mail). Ranks those against prices the user already has: their insurance copay and any pharmacy quote or coupon they mention. Use it when the user asks what a medication costs, where it is cheapest, whether the generic or paying cash beats their insurance, or whether a quote is fair. Takes the drug as the user says it (brand or generic, with strength if known, as in "Lipitor 20 mg" or "metformin ER 500") and a quantity. When the drug comes in several strengths or forms the result lists them instead of prices: ask the user which one is on their bottle, then call again. When no open source lists the drug, the result says so and links coupon sites: don't call again for it. Turn the result into a short answer: lead with the cheapest real option and its price, say what the generic saves over the brand, and whether their copay or quote is above a fair cash price. NADAC rows are what pharmacies pay, a benchmark, not a price the user can pay. Coupon sites (GoodRx, SingleCare) are linked, not fetched. The result is informational: never suggest changing the drug, strength or dose to save money; that is for the prescriber or pharmacist. Its output ends with a [chart] line, which the chat draws for the user (each option's price): don't repeat every number or redraw it with generate_chart unless the user asks for an image file.
author: Hannes Hapke

drug.description: The medication, brand or generic, optionally with strength and form: "atorvastatin", "Lipitor 20 mg", "metformin ER 500 mg".

strength.description: The strength, when not in drug, such as "20 mg" or "0.05 mg/ml".

form.description: The form, when it matters, such as "tablet", "capsule", "ER", "solution" or "patch".

quantity.description: How many units to price: tablets or capsules, or mL or g for liquids and creams (NADAC's pricing unit).

copay.description: What the user's insurance charges them for this fill, to compare with cash prices.

known_prices.description: Prices the user already has, such as a pharmacy's quote or a coupon.

source.description: Where the price is from, such as "CVS with GoodRx".

quantity.description: The quantity it is for, when not the same as quantity.
